extracted.intended_audience: international doctoral applicants seeking DAAD doctoral scholarships for research/PhD in Germany
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and formal requirements for international applicants to the DAAD Doctoral Programmes scholarship: eligibility rules, required application documents, selection criteria (qualification, research quality, applicant potential), funding details, and procedural instructions for submitting an online application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who can apply / academic degree requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You can apply if you have above-average qualifications and you completed your Master's degree or Diplom, or in exceptional cases a Bachelor's degree, at the latest by the time the funding period begins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must usually hold a Master's/Diplom; exceptional Bachelor's cases may be considered. Degree must be completed before funding starts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-since-graduation limits
rubrics_metrics.description: As a rule, applicants should not have graduated any longer than six years before the application deadline. If you have already started your doctorate, the start of the doctorate should not be longer than 3 years ago.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check Important Scholarship Information / Section A, point 2 for details and possible exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residence restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Your application cannot be considered, if you have been resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residence in Germany exceeding 15 months at the deadline disqualifies the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field-specific exceptions (medicine, veterinary, dentistry)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applicants from the fields of human medicine, veterinary medicine and dentistry, other regulations are applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to www.daad.de/extrainfo for the particular additional regulations that apply to these fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of projects that can be funded
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding is provided for a doctoral project at a state or state-recognised institution of higher education or a non-university research institute in Germany: either an individual project supervised by a university teacher (doctoral supervisor) or participation in a structured doctoral study programme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify whether your project is individual or part of a structured programme; provide appropriate supporting documents (supervision letter or module plan/proof of contacts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research phases outside Germany
rubrics_metrics.description: Research phases outside Germany can be funded if these are critical for successful completion of your doctoral degree and should constitute no more than one quarter of the anticipated total funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must provide details about planned visits in your study plan and time schedule in your application documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of funding and assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding is provided for a maximum of four years; grants are initially awarded for a maximum of three years. Academic achievements are assessed annually, and continuation/extension to a fourth year depends on positive assessment and feasibility to complete doctorate within a reasonable period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The length of the funding period is decided by a selection committee and depends on your project and study plan. Funding must begin in 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial benefits (standard package)
rubrics_metrics.description: Monthly payments of €1,400; payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance cover; travel allowance; annual research allowance of €460.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional benefits may be available after the start of funding under certain circumstances (see further items).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional financial benefits and special subsidies
rubrics_metrics.description: Under certain circumstances, applicants may apply after the start of funding for: monthly rent subsidy, monthly allowance for accompanying family members, and subsidies for justified additional costs due to disability or chronic illness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether and to what extent subsidies are paid will be reviewed and determined individually (see Important Scholarship Information / section F, points 3, 8, 9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language support and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: DAAD offers payment of course fees for an online language course after receipt of the Scholarship Award Letter; possibly a pre-start language course (2, 4 or 6 months) if decided by DAAD depending on language skills and project; allowance for a personally chosen German course during the grant period; reimbursement of TestDaF or DSH test fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a language course scholarship is granted and the working language at the host institute is German, participation is compulsory. Tests can be taken in home country after award or in Germany during funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party benefits crediting
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefits from third parties are partially credited towards the DAAD scholarship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Important Scholarship Information / section F, point 6 for details on how third-party funding affects the DAAD scholarship amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process and review body
rubrics_metrics.description: An independent selection committee consisting of specialist scientists reviews applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The selection committee assesses applications according to the stated selection criteria (Qualification; Quality of research project; Potential of applicant) and gives due consideration to equal opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criterion — Qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic achievements (grade point average, development of grades); academic progress; knowledge of the language(s) of instruction or working language(s); if applicable, scholarly achievements after graduation (e.g., publications, lectures, conference papers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide transcripts, degree certificates, and evidence of scholarly achievements. Language skills are evaluated relative to the project's working language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criterion — Quality of research project
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of research proposal and preparation (originality, topicality and relevance of the project, choice of host institution and first contacts); feasibility and consistency of study plan and schedule; incorporation of project within the overall doctorate (in terms of content and time), if relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a detailed proposal (prepared and formulated by yourself) and a study plan/time schedule; explain host choice and how the project fits into the doctorate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criterion — Potential of applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Career prospects: significance of the research project and stay in Germany for further academic, professional and personal development. Motivation: academic and personal reasons for wanting to visit Germany; German language skills (if different from working language). Non-study-related activities: non-study-related knowledge and skills, civic engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the expected impact on your career and personal development; include civic engagement and other extracurricular strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunities consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The selection committee gives due consideration to equal opportunities; applicants can provide relevant information in the application form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relevant, include information in the application to assist the committee's equal-opportunity assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application documents — core list
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents to be submitted: full curriculum vitae in tabular form (max. 3 pages); list of publications (max. 10 pages), if applicable; description of academic and personal reasons for your planned project in Germany (letter of motivation: 1-2 pages); a proposal and description of previous research work (max. 10 pages in total).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letter of motivation should address: 'What do you hope to gain from your project in Germany (personally, professionally, for your career)?' Upload documents under the specified portal sections (study project/motivation; research project).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application documents — supervision and programme proof
rubrics_metrics.description: For individual projects: schedule for planned research work (agreed with academic supervisor) and letter confirming supervision by the doctoral supervisor. For structured doctoral programmes: module plan, proof of existing contacts to the coordinator, letter of admission (may be submitted later).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload confirmation from the academic host under 'acceptance of host institution' and module plan under 'schedule' when applicable. See Important Scholarship Information / section C, point 3 for supervisor confirmation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application documents — ethics and degree proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Declaration from the scientific supervisor in Germany on safety-relevant and ethical aspects of the research project; university degree certificate indicating final grade(s) (may be submitted later but must be provided before grant-supported research begins if not available at application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload the ethics/safety declaration under 'Scientific ethics/research safety'. If degree certificate is pending at application, submit as soon as available before funding starts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application documents — recommendation(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: One recent, supporting letter of recommendation from a university teacher which provides information about your qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generate the recommendation form in the DAAD Portal during the application period, send it to your university teacher to complete, then upload it under 'Letter of Recommendation'. See the tab 'Submitting an application' for instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional supporting documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Other documents which support your application (example: certificates of employment, proof of practical training/internships and voluntary commitment etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include as appropriate to strengthen your case; these are not mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting, translations and file rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificates, proof of credits, certifications and translations may be scanned in non-certified form and uploaded. If you submit documents in your national language, include German or English translations. You can only upload PDF files to the portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DAAD reserves the right to request certified copies. Upload translations together with the original-language document. Scan paper documents to PDF before upload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for this scholarship programme are possible in the period June until the stated application deadline. The DAAD portal closes at 24.00 hrs. (CET or CEST) on the last application day. The portal is accessible only while the current application period is running.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit all required documents via the DAAD portal by the deadline. If sending documents by post, send as soon as possible; the postmark date serves as proof of dispatch. Do not rely on submitting on the final date in case of technical problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness rule and data handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Incomplete applications cannot be considered. Your application is only valid if you submit all the required documents to the DAAD portal by the application deadline. The application documents remain with the DAAD; personal data is saved in accordance with Federal Data Protection Act and EU Data Protection Regulation as needed to process the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you upload every required document before the portal closes and be aware that DAAD retains application documents and processes personal data according to law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portal technical support procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Register in the DAAD portal, generate the recommendation form during the application period, prepare/scan documents to PDF, fill out the online application and upload attachments. If you have technical questions not resolved locally, contact portal@daad.de or call the technical portal hotline (weekdays 9-12 and 14-16 CET/CEST).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The usage of the application portal is limited on mobile devices — use a desktop computer. Consider processing times when contacting support.
